''' Robert H. Shapiro''' (July 18, 1935 &ndash; August 21, 2004) was an American chemist and the first [[Provost (education)|academic provost]] of the [[United States Naval Academy]].

==Education and career==

After serving with both the [[United States Navy]] and the [[United States Marine Corps]], Shapiro earned degrees in chemistry and pharmacy at the [[University of Connecticut]], and then went to [[Stanford University]], where he received a Ph.D. in chemistry.<ref name="obit">{{cite web
 |title       = Obituary of Robert H. Shapiro
 |url         = https://www.cu.edu/sg/messages/3787.html
 |accessdate  = 2008-09-28
 |url-status  = dead
 |archiveurl  = https://web.archive.org/web/20060922090536/http://www.cu.edu/sg/messages/3787.html
 |archivedate = 2006-09-22
}}</ref> In 1965 he became professor at the [[University of Colorado at Boulder]], and from 1980 until his retirement in 1989 he worked at the [[James Madison University]] as dean of the College of Letters and Sciences and as vice-provost of the university.<ref name="obit"/> He then became dean, and then provost, at the [[United States Naval Academy]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Weil |first=Martin |last2=Leff |first2=Lisa |date=1990-02-25 |title=NAVAL ACADEMY RELIEVES HEAD OF DEPARTMENT |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/local/1990/02/25/naval-academy-relieves-head-of-department/a61cf96b-7d4f-473f-82c7-7fce4b6c02ec/ |access-date=2024-01-25 |work=Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> Shapiro served as the academy's chief academic officer until his retirement in 1998.<ref name="obit"/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty and Staff: Deans and Registrars, 1966-2002|url=https://www.usna.edu/Library/sca/arc-findingaids/view.php?f=RG405-10_faculty_deans |access-date=2026-05-23|publication-date=March 2017|publisher=United States Naval Academy |website=www.usna.edu |language=en}}</ref>

He served as the editor of the journal Organic Mass Spectroscopy (now the [[Journal of Mass Spectrometry]]) for ten years. The [[Shapiro reaction]], which he discovered in 1967, is named for him.<ref>{{Citation |chapter=Shapiro reaction |date=2006 |title=Name Reactions: A Collection of Detailed Reaction Mechanisms |pages=529–530 |editor-last=Li |editor-first=Jie Jack |chapter-url=https://doi.org/10.1007/3-540-30031-7_241 |access-date=2024-01-25 |place=Berlin, Heidelberg |publisher=Springer |language=en |doi=10.1007/3-540-30031-7_241 |isbn=978-3-540-30031-1|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref>
